# Tripadvisor.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/tripadvisor-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/tripadvisor-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects data from tripadvisor.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape TripAdvisor.com (2025 Updated)](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-tripadvisor)
- **Code:** [`tripadvisor.py`](tripadvisor.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Hotel pages](results/hotels.json) · [Search pages](results/search.json) · [Location pages](results/location.json)

## What it scrapes

- TripAdvisor search for finding hotels from search queries.
  e.g. <https://www.tripadvisor.com/Hotels-g190311-Malta-Hotels.html>
- TripAdvisor hotel listing details:
  e.g. <https://www.tripadvisor.com/Hotels-g190311-Malta-Hotels.html>
    - hotel info: description, rating, features etc.
    - prices
    - reviews

## Functions

- `scrape_location_data(query)` → `List[LocationData]`: scrape search location data from a given query. e.g. "New York" will return us TripAdvisor's location details for this query
- `scrape_search(search_url, max_pages=None)` → `List[Preview]`: scrape search results of a search query
- `scrape_hotel(url, max_review_pages=None)` → `Dict`: Scrape hotel data and reviews

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import tripadvisor


async def main():
    location_data = await tripadvisor.scrape_location_data(query="Malta")
    search = await tripadvisor.scrape_search(
        search_url="https://www.tripadvisor.com/Hotels-g60763-oa30-New_York_City_New_York-Hotels.html",
        max_pages=2,
    )
    hotel = await tripadvisor.scrape_hotel(
        "https://www.tripadvisor.com/Hotel_Review-g190327-d264936-Reviews-1926_Hotel_Spa-Sliema_Island_of_Malta.html",
        max_review_pages=3,
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`LocationData`**: `localizedName`, `url`, `HOTELS_URL`, `ATTRACTIONS_URL`, `RESTAURANTS_URL`, `placeType`, `latitude`, `longitude`
- **`Preview`**: `url`, `name`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`tripadvisor.py`](tripadvisor.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/tripadvisor-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_hotel_scraping`, `test_location_data_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
